leadIn.title: Lead-In & Context: Irregular Verbs
leadIn.content: Past events: Yesterday I went to the market, ate an apple, and bought a book. Many common verbs do not use -ed in the past.

meaningCheck.question: Function check: What is the primary purpose of using Irregular Verbs?
options: To express clear, level-appropriate meaning in structured context
To translate sentences word-for-word from another language
It is an obsolete form never used by native speakers
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · This structure provides explicit grammatical function and clarity.

meaningCheck.question: Form check: Does correct usage of Irregular Verbs require matching subject, verb, and modifier agreements?
options: No, agreement rules are optional in English
Yes, matching grammatical forms ensures natural, accurate communication
Agreement only matters in formal academic writing
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · Accurate form and agreement choices prevent misunderstandings.

form.title: Form & Structure: Irregular Verbs
form.content: Base verb -> Past simple form (go -> went, eat -> ate, buy -> bought). Must be memorized as special past forms.

pronunciation.title: Pronunciation Notes: Irregular Verbs
pronunciation.content: Spoken stress, weak forms, intonation, and articulation patterns for Irregular Verbs.

controlledPractice.question: Past of 'be'?
controlledPractice.explanation: Be → was/were, the most irregular verb of all.

controlledPractice.question: Past of 'cut'?
controlledPractice.explanation: Cut doesn't change at all in the past simple.
